en: "...Thirsty. Want water...{w}...Cold. Dark...{w}Where is this place?... Want water..."{w}
note: Sapling speaks in all-katakana; rendered as halting, broken English rather than caps.

en: "No matter where I plant it, it's like this the whole time...{w}Even I'm starting to feel kind of--"{w}{p}"It's just too pitiful to watch... I'm losing all my confidence here."{w}
"I know! You guys are adventurers, right?{w}
note: No closing quote in source; continues in row 803.

en:
{0E}"I know! You guys are adventurers, right?{0F}
Could you go and plant this sapling somewhere nice for me, in my place?"{w}{p}"Please, I'm counting on you...{w}It doesn't seem happy here, and I've got the other plants to look after, too..."{w}
"Huh? A visitor? That's rare, for someone who only ever keeps plants company... Wait, aren't you the guys from that time?"{w}
note: Hanoi teases Chirocco (first sentence), then recognizes the party.

en: "Oh, Hanoi. You know them?"{w}
"Well, sort of."{w}
"Could you ask them too, Hanoi?{w}I'm thinking of entrusting the sapling to them."{w}

"That's a pretty bright idea, for you, Chirocco. We've both got plenty on our plates, after all."{w}{p}"I bet that sapling would say that's what it wants, too.{w}Definitely. Probably."{w}{p}"Besides, they seem to come by here a lot, but they're adventurers, technically, right?"{w}{p}"I heard my village got saved from a tight spot, too, by some no-name adventurers from who-knows-where."{w}{p}"So if we leave it to folks of the same sort, it'll be fine for sure.{w}...Maybe. Possibly."{w}{p}"Let's see... That place might work, seeing as it's a forest that's nothing but trees.{w}The conditions are perfect."{w}
note: ore-ra isogashii read as Hanoi + Chirocco both being busy. Hanoi talks to Chirocco about the party in 3rd person ('they'). Running joke of hedges kept (kitto. tabun / ...kamo. moshikashitara).

en: "Really?{w}Thank goodness. Now that sapling will finally be saved."{w}
"Well, I guess this counts as helping people too?{w}...Anyway, we're counting on you, my fellow adventurers!"{w}
note: boukensha shokun -> 'my fellow adventurers' (jokey-formal address).

en:
[Key Item]
Received Chatty Sapling.{w}
note: Item name oshaberi na naegi -> 'Chatty Sapling' (new). Format follows [Key Item]/Obtained X; uketotta -> Received.

en: "My place is in 'Perpeco Village.' It's all forest around there, so it's just right, isn't it?{w}For the exact spot, ask somebody in the village."{w}
note: uchi = Hanoi's home/family; Hanoi is from Perpeco (ties to row 808 'my village').

en: "I'm counting on you!"{w}
"Hey, how's it going?{w}Take a look around the garden if you like. It's good for the soul, right?"{w}{p}"So, how about it? Have you decided where to plant the sapling?"{w}
"Hey, you guys.{w}Did you plant the sapling for me? By the spring in Perpeco Forest, you say?"{w}{p}"That's a great spot. You did a fine job."{w}
"I'm so glad.{w}Now I can finally concentrate on building the garden, too. Thank you."{w}
"If there's a plant you can't figure out, just ask me. I'll brag a little: I know most of them. Anything in this garden, leave it to me."{w}
Rookie
note: shinjin = Madulay's apprentice at the shipyard; gender unknown.

en: "Hm? What business would adventurers have in a place like this?"{w}
What will you do?
note: Same rendering as wmap slice_20 row 1564.

en: "Hm? I see. See ya{w}
note: No closing quote or period in source; kept unfinished.

en: Ask about alchemy items
"Alchemy, huh... Man, that's a tough one.{w}Boss Madulaaay!"{w}
note: oyassan -> 'Boss' (gender-neutral; Madulay's gender is unknown in glossary).

en: Madulay

"What was that!?
You still ain't learned somethin' that basic!?"{w}{p}"Good timin'.{w}I'll teach you folks too, so listen up good."{w}
note: First page yells at the Rookie; second page addresses the party.

en: "What I know comes from years of hard-earned experience. I ain't givin' it away for free.{w}But it'll pay off every time, guaranteed."{w}{p}"If there's anything else you wanna know about alchemy items, come on by anytime.{w}
note: No closing quote in source; continues in row 827.

en:
{0E}"If there's anything else you wanna know about alchemy items, come on by anytime.{0F}
Oi, rookie! You'd better damn well learn it this time!"{w}

"Eep!
I'm real sorry, Boss!"{w}
Look at the ship
"Ah, crap! Hurry, get outta here!{w}Otherwise Boss Madulay's gonna...{w}
note: Speaker field empty; context shows it is the Rookie. No closing quote in source.

en: "Oi! Who the hell's walkin' in here without permission!?{w}Rookie, what're you doin'!? Throw those adventurers out, pronto!"{w}
"Aye aye!!{w}C'mon! Out, quick! I'm beggin' you!{w}Boss Madulay's thunder is comin'!!"{w}
note: Speaker = Rookie (context). kaminari kept as 'thunder' (temper). | Editorial: "Aye, sir" gendered Madulay (glossary unknown); "Aye aye" is the same loanword sense, matches 1009.

en:
"Oi! You there, rookie!{w}Why've you got your hands stuffed in your pockets!?{w}Those are for your tools, ya damn fool!"{w}{p}"Listen up! Don't you slack off on the job!
It won't end with just you gettin' hurt!"{w}
"Anybody dawdlin' around gets thrown in the mana furnace!!"{w}
note: makouro -> 'mana furnace' (new term; the ship's engine furnace).

en: "Hey!{w}Draggin' around long stuff like swords and spears -- what if you bang 'em into the equipment!?"{w}{p}"Breakin' stuff is what you adventurers are good for.{w}Buildin' stuff is what us craftsfolk are good for.{w}There's no work for you here!"{w}
"Useless lot! Get the hell out!!"{w}
"You came back!?{w}Just what's a bunch of two-bit adventurers findin' so amusin'...{w}
note: No closing quote in source; continues in row 838.
Rinos Undersea Volcano = new place name. 'the kid' keeps the Rookie gender-neutral.

en: "The coarse stone came through fine. But...{w}the medium stone and the fine stone, now...{w}Those two. ...Please."{w}
note: Whetstone grades: ara-to = coarse, naka-to = medium, shiage-to = finishing.

en: "The Medium Whetstone and the Fine Whetstone, those two.{w}Maintenance tools matter most, right after your work tools......... I'm countin' on ya."{w}
note: Capitalised as key-item names (chap slice_017 rows 1347-1348 are their pickup messages).

en: "Medium Whetstone and Fine Whetstone, both of 'em, all right.{w}Thanks, you really bailed me out."{w}{p}"I coulda just bought new whetstones, sure, but the stones from these parts suit my tools just right."{w}
note: koko no toishi read as 'the local stones' (from the volcano near Roscadil).

en: "...These tools have been in my family for three generations. I wanna take good care of 'em.{w}You really saved me there{w}
note: No closing quote or period in source; kept.

en: "...Hey, you folks, what d'you make of this thing?{w}Pretty over-the-top, ain't it?{w}...It's a warship."{w}{p}"My granddad and my old man were both magic airship shipwrights.{w}So I'm buildin' this thing just like they did."{w}{p}"I take pride in this work, and I'm gonna get this thing flyin', no matter what."{w}
note: makuutei (magic airship) = new term. Grandfather/father genders are explicit in the source.

en: "A warship... huh.{w}Sinful business, this, when all I want is to see this thing fly..."{w}{p}"Empress Rianna is a person of principle.{w}So she won't go puttin' this thing to wicked use, I'd say."{w}
note: Queen (joou) is explicit in source, so 'she' for Rianna.

en: "...Hah! No use grumblin' about it!{w}I'll just do my job, and do it right, that's all!"{w}
"Oi, you lot! Put some fire in it!{w}Anybody dawdlin' around gets thrown in the mana furnace!!"{w}
note: Addressed to the shipyard workers.

en: "Shape up, the lot of you! I won't stand for anyone goin' slack on the job!"{w}{p}"Anybody dawdlin' around gets thrown in the mana furnace!"{w}
Old Woman

"Oh?
Out for a stroll too, are you?"{w}{p}"Lovely night view, isn't it? Ukiki!"{w}{p}"What's this, you came up here without knowing who I am? You lot are a funny bunch.{w}Ukiki!"{w}
note: ukiki = Shimerief's monkey-like cackle, kept as a verbal tic.

en: Shimerief
note: New name (romanised shi-me-ri-e-fu). Also appears untranslated in chap slice_006.

en: "Shimerief. That's my name."{w}
"Here's an old-timer's tale from long ago. Keep me company a little while."{w}
"...When I was young, I wandered here, there and everywhere with a sword in hand."{w}{p}"Always on about who's strong, and how do I stack up."{w}
"Good with a sword? More skilled than anyone?{w}Compared to who, exactly?{w}
note: No closing quote in source; continues in row 855.

en: "...The ones who come begging me to teach 'em are all like that, too...{w}Honestly, it's as silly as it gets."{w}
"......Come to think of it, there was one interesting kid lately... now who was it..."{w}
note: omoshiroi ko: gender unknown, kept as 'kid'.

en: "When all you do is swing a sword,{w}it's 'Am I stronger than anyone? What is strength?'{w}That's all you end up thinking about."{w}{p}"That's when I met a certain sage."{w}{p}"So I counted my lucky stars and asked about this and that...{w}
note: No closing quote in source; continues in row 859.

en:
{0E}"So I counted my lucky stars and asked about this and that...{0F}
and it was like, 'Geez, there's no end to any of this...'{w}Overcomplicated, and no limit to it, either."{w}
"It's ridiculous beyond words.{w}Living, dying, killing, being killed, winning, losing, strong, weak."{w}
"All of that, every last bit of it,{w}is just in your head. Ukiki!"{w}
note: tada no ki no sei -> 'just in your head'.

en: "I've been waiting for you. You lot have nothing better to do anyway, right?{w}Keep me company tonight."{w}{p}"Come on, hurry up and get ready.{w}We're headed for the Blue Cave. Ukiki!"{w}
note: Blue Cave as in wmap slice_03 row 235. | Accuracy: subject restored (I've been waiting).

en: "What are you doing? We're headed for the Blue Cave. Ukiki!"{w}
"Seen a swordswoman wearing a beard, have you? I'm the one who gave her that, you know. Suited her, didn't it? Ukiki!"{w}
note: hige -> 'beard' to match the key item 'Sword Elder's Beard' (chap slice_001 row 66), which this likely refers to; 'mustache' is possible.

en: No one seems to be here.{w}

"Welcome in~!{w}Welcome to Toner's Armory~!"{w}{p}"Oh, are you maybe... from Algrantz?{w}I knew it! You bought that at my mom's shop, didn't you?"{w}{p}"I thought it looked familiar!{w}Please give Toner's Armory your business, too!"{w}
note: Toner no bugu-ten / Toner bugu-ten -> 'Toner's Armory' (new). Mom = Gia (Kembeck's Shop). Toner's gender unknown: no pronouns.

en: "Hmm~ hmm hmm hmm-hmm~ hmm~~...{w}Oh, welcome in~!"{w}{p}"What do you all think of this outfit?{w}Doesn't it get you super excited?{w}It's so fluffy, and frilly, and silky!"{w}
note: Humming; music-note symbol replaced by '~' (ASCII). wakuwaku = Toner's catchword, rendered with 'thrill/thrilling' throughout.

en: "...What should I do, it's merchandise...{w}But just for a little bit... Hmmm...{w}
note: No closing quote in source.

en: "Yep! I've decided!{w}I'll save up my allowance and buy it!"{w}
"Eh heh heh heh... All right! Time to work my hardest, all for the excitement!"{w}
"And you all, too,{w}if you find anything exciting, please{w}bring it to my shop, okay?"{w}
"...........So exciiiting-- waaaah!!{w}
note: The squeal turns into a shriek on noticing the party. No closing quote; continues in row 873.

en:
{0E}"...........So exciiiting-- waaaah!!{0F}
Wh-- How long have you all been here!? Th-this, this isn't what it looks like!"{w}
"Okay, if you asked me how it's different, I'd be stuck, but it's not what it looks like! Huh, what am I even talking about... I was just trying on some exciting clothes, that's all!"{w}
"But even if I say 'trying,' it's merchandise, okay!? I'd never... like, actually wear it... never...{w}.............................................."{w}
"...W-welcome iiin~! Welcome to Toner's Armory!!{w}......Waaaaah!!"{w}
note: uwaan = crying wail.

en: Toner was nowhere to be seen.{w}Instead, for some reason, a blonde girl was standing there.{w}
note: 'girl' is the narration's own word for the figure (it is Toner in costume, slice_12 rows 880-887); no gender implied for Toner.

en: "Oh, good evening, everyone! You came back!{w}Welcome to Toner's Arm-- ...Oh."{w}
note: Speaker ??? = Toner as 'Safi'. Cut off mid-word as in source. | Editorial: "to see us" was added (accuracy flag); Toner runs the shop alone.

en: "...No, I mean-- I'm Safi! Safi!"{w}
note: safi -> 'Safi' (new name; Toner's alter ego, see slice_12).

en: Safi?
note: New name: sa-fi romanized 'Safi' (not in glossary; PLAYER.CSV row 113 lists it as a recruitable character). Toner's dress-up alter ego.

en: "Toner's a pal of mine! I-I mean, a dear friend of mine! I-I'm Safi! I'm Safi, really! I'm Safiii! ......Auuu..."{w}
note: Source joke: Toner says 'Toner wa boku no tomodachi' with the boyish boku, then corrects 'not boku, watashi'. English has no gendered 'I', so the slip is rendered as a rough 'pal of mine' corrected to a dainty 'dear friend of mine'.

en: Toner?
"...T-To-- I mean, I'm Safi, and...{w}Um... it's totally obvious, isn't it? ...Uuu...{w}...Keep it a secret, okay? That I'm Safi..."{w}
note: 'bo... ja nakute watashi' = another boku/watashi slip; rendered as Toner nearly blurting out the real name. The last clause switches back to boku (giving up the act); 'That I'm Safi' carries the confession.

en:
"I mean, clothes that are all fluffy and frilly
are just so exciting...{w}
note: No closing quote in source; row 885 echoes this text inside {0E}..{0F}. wakuwaku (Toner's catchword) = 'exciting/excited' throughout.
Echo of 884; keep both identical.

en: "...Sigh, oh well, can't be helped...{w}Oh, I know!{w}
note: No closing quote in source; continues in 887.
Echo of 886 with its {w} turned into \n, as the source does. wakuwaku Safi = 'Exciting Safi' (stage-name style).

en: Safi
"But... actually, there's something missing.{w}Do you know about Blue Rain?{w}I want it so, so badly."{w}

"Blue Rain is what I've always dreamed of,
and I've been searching and searching for it, but...{w}Ahh... Blue Rain..."{w}{p}"Everyone, please.{w}Exciting Safi needs Blue Rain!"{w}
note: Safi slips into boku again here ('boku no akogare'); not reproducible in English, left unmarked.

en: "Otherwise... Safi will...{w}...Oh, wait here just a moment, okay?"{w}
note: Sentence deliberately broken off; completed by Toner in 893 after the costume change.

en: With a patter of footsteps, Safi ducked into the back of the shop.{w}A little later, Safi came back as Toner.{w}
note: Narration; 'Toner no sugata de' = in Toner's form/clothes.

en: "...never get to be exciting!{w}Please, I'm counting on you!"{w}
note: Completes Safi's unfinished line in 891 ('ja nai to... Safi wa...' + 'wakuwaku ni narenai'), so the English opens mid-sentence with an ellipsis.

en: Toner had apparently gone to the trouble of changing clothes just to say that.{w}His (her?) eyes held a deadly earnest look.{w}
note: 'kare (kanojo?)' is the source's own joke about Toner's gender; translated literally as 'His (her?)'. No other pronoun is used for Toner anywhere in this slice.

en:
"I really, really need Blue Rain,
so I'm counting on you, okay!?"{w}
note: Repeat-visit line.

en:
"Yaaay! It's Blue Rain!{w}Now I can get more and more excited! Thank you so much!"{w}{p}"Oh, I know! In return, I'll fix it so you can secretly buy
something only knights are allowed to buy!"{w}
note: kishi-san shika kacchaikenai shina: 'knights' kept lowercase/generic -- unclear whether this means a character class or Roscadil's knights; check against the class list. | Editorial: "even more and more" ungrammatical.

en: {0E}         * Elven Chain +1 now in stock *{0F}{w}
note: Item name Elven Chain +1 (ITEM.CSV:273); align with ITEM.CSV once translated. Banner style follows earlier slices.

en:
"That's my thanks for the Blue Rain!{w}Ahh, Blue Rain... these stripes...
They get me so excited already!!"{w}
note: Stripes: glossary note says Blue Rain is blue-striped underwear.

en:
"Okay, I'm going to change now,
so face the other way, okay?"{w}

You got a push on the back
and were spun right around to face the other way.{w}
Toner's Voice
"No turning around, okay?"
note: Prompt text above the choices 903/924; quotes kept as in source.

en: Turn around
note: Menu choice.

en: You turned around anyway.{w}
note: 'furimuite mita' = tried turning around (against instructions); 'anyway' carries the -te miru.

en: "Waaah!?!?"{w}
"No! Wait till I'm done changing!!"{w}
Clutching the half-shed clothes close, Toner was making some kind of fuss.{w}That flustered face was adorable, too.{w}{p}...On a whim, you let your gaze drift downward.{w}
note: mune-moto ni kaki-atsume = gathering the clothes to the chest; 'close' used to avoid a pronoun for Toner. | Editorial: present tense in past-tense narration made consistent.

en: "Where are you looking!?{w}Face the other way! Mooo-ooo-ooo~~!!{w}Seriously... moooooo~~~..."{w}
note: mou~ (exasperated 'jeez') spelled 'moo' so that 910's cow pun still works.

en:
Toner was going "moo, moo" like a cow...
but wasn't what you'd just seen an elephant?{w}...The facts of the matter had to be verified.{w}{p}Straining your eyes, you found something.{w}
note: zou (elephant) = Japanese euphemism for a penis ('little elephant'); kept as 'elephant' with the cow/elephant contrast, not explained. Crude joke kept at full strength. | Editorial: tense made consistent with the past-tense narration.
? Mace = the game's unidentified-item name (ITEM.CSV col 5 '?Mace' form); keep identical to the item table's unidentified name once translated. Phallic gag continues 910.

en: "Um, hey... excuse me...?"{w}
Appraise it!
note: Menu choice parodying the identify prompt ('kantei shimasu ka' with ! instead of ?). kantei = Wizardry-style identify; 'Identify' chosen here because it mocks the item-identify UI (pilot uses 'appraise' for Gia's shop service). | lead: [JP] = appraise (corpus decision)

en: ...Appraising.{w}
note: Parody of the identify messages; keep in step with the UI's identify strings once translated. | lead: [JP] = appraise (corpus decision)
Source is a string of symbols (incl. male/female signs); replaced with an ASCII grawlix.

en: ...Appraising.{w}{p}Oops! You touched it!{w}
note: sawatte shimatta! = the classic Wizardry identify-failure message (touching a cursed item), here a groping gag. | lead: [JP] = appraise (corpus decision)
Symbol scream; ASCII grawlix.

en: Appraising!{w}
note: | lead: [JP] = appraise (corpus decision)

en: ...Appraised!!{w}
note: | lead: [JP] = appraise (corpus decision)
No {w} in source.

en: "That is quiiiite enough!!"{w}
note: ii-kagen ni shite kudasai with stretched ii.

en: ...You got scolded.{w}

Already thoroughly satisfied, you quietly turned your back
and waited for Toner to finish changing.{w}
note: Whose changing is left implicit in Japanese; Toner's, by the scene.

en: Keep waiting
note: Menu choice.

en: You kept waiting, just as you were told.{w}
......{w}It seemed Toner had finished changing.{w}
note: Editorial: tense made consistent with the past-tense narration.

en: "And so -- it's Safi!"{w}
"Having you watch me while I changed... that's embarrassing..."{w}
note: Peek-branch line: 'kigaeru tokoro kara mirareru' = being seen from the changing onward.

en:
"Safi wants to get even more excited.{w}So, everyone... from now on,
I'm counting on you!"{w}{p}"Oh, but as for Mom...{w}not a w-o-r-d, okay?{w}
note: na-i-sho spelled out syllable by syllable -> 'not a w-o-r-d'. No closing quote at the end; 930 echoes the last page.
Echo of 929's last page with its {w} turned into \n.

en: {0E}  * Safi has been registered at the Training Hall *{0F}{w}
note: Training Hall per glossary.
The 'every night' innuendo is the source's; kept as is.

en: "Welcome!{w}Toner is out at the moment~!{w}
note: No closing quote; 934 echoes it.
Echo of 933.

en:
"Welcome!{w}Oh, you came!
I got so tired of waiting!"{w}
"Wh-wh-wh-what!?"{w}
note: Lone line in 91242-ROS_TONER_TALK, no speaker box; presumably Toner reacting.

en:
"Who goes there!?"{w}{p}"Adventurers of unknown origin
are not permitted in the palace!{w}Leave before you are cut down!!"{w}
note: Roscadil palace guard.
heika -> 'Her Majesty': Rianna is called an empress (jotei) by the narration in row 949, so 'Her' is from the source, not assumed. Flagged anyway (glossary gender 'unknown').

en: You got thrown out.{w}
note: Shared by 3 places.

en: "Who goes there!?{w}Adventurers of unknown origin are not..."{w}
note: Cut off by Branon in 941; shortened version of 937.

en: "Ah, now, hold on, hold on."{w}
note: Speaker ??? = Branon (named in 942).

en: "These people are my guests, would you suppose!"{w}
note: Branon's misused deeroka tag rendered 'would you suppose' as in slice 10. He uses watashi here instead of wagahai; invisible in English.

en:
"Ugh, Executor Branon...{w}What are you doing here?
Shouldn't you be having your tea time?"{w}
note: Branon-sama -> 'Executor Branon' (title from slice 10) to avoid gendered Lord/Sir. The guard's 'oyoroshii no de' is mock-polite; rendered as a mildly snide question.

en:
"I wish to introduce them
to Her Majesty Rianna, would you suppose."{w}
note: See 938 for 'Her Majesty'.

en: "Uh, is that so...{w}Go right ahead, suit yourself... Er, um, salute..."{w}
"Now then, come along."{w}

Paying the half-hearted salute no mind at all,
Branon strode right on into the palace.{w}
note: bimyou na keirei = an iffy, half-hearted salute.

en: "Is Her Majesty Rianna about, would you suppose!"{w}

When Branon opened the doors of the audience chamber,
there sat an empress of dignified bearing.{w}
note: jotei = empress (source).

en: Rianna
"What is it, Branon?{w}You, coming to the palace of your own accord?{w}Have you lost your mind?"{w}

"No, no, Your Majesty!{w}Your humble Branon's intelligence-gathering among the common folk
has finally borne fruit, would you suppose!"{w}
note: 'Branon-me' = self-deprecating; 'Your humble Branon'.

en: "Oh? Speak, then."{w}

note: New term: makuutei -> 'magic airship' (lowercase generic; Rianna names the ship Meatrif in slice 13 row 962). Coordinate with slice 13.

en: "Who are they? Adventurers?"{w}
"That they are, would you suppose!"{w}
"Very well.{w}Whatever you know cannot amount to much anyway."{w}
note: Rianna permits it because Branon's knowledge is limited. | Editorial: Rianna voice, no contractions in composed speech.

en:
"To build the magic airship we need
'Selcoa Paint,' 'Celestial Readings'
and a 'Wing Soul,' would you suppose!"{w}{p}"How about putting them to work
obtaining those, would you suppose!"{w}
note: Item names from pilot rows 5-7 (Selcoa Paint / Celestial Survey Results / Wing Soul). Japanese single-bracket titles -> single quotes per brief. | Proof: commas moved inside quotes (file convention).

en: "Hmm."{w}

"They braved danger and hardship without a care, and brought me something that made my very tongue sing, would you suppose!"{w}{p}"With drive like that, they are sure to gather what the magic airship needs as well, would you suppose!"{w}
note: Branon pitching the party to Rianna (cf. 958). Branon's misplaced 'de arou ka/darou ka' tag kept as 'would you suppose', per slice_10. [JP] = impress the palate (the sweets quest, rows 774-782).

en: "I see.{w}True, anyone able to satisfy your demands might well prove useful."{w}

"Very well, I will tell you.{w}Surely you know of the strange events at the Palace of the Sun?"{w}{p}"We are now pushing ahead with a plan to fly to the Palace of the Sun in a flying ship called the Meatrif -- a 'magic airship' -- and take back the sun from the Kin of Darkness."{w}{p}"But the things we need are proving hard to come by.{w}The first thing we want is 'Selcoa Paint.'"{w}{p}"It is a paint that readily takes on magic power.{w}Coat a ship with it the proper way, and even light materials gain all the strength they need."{w}{p}"We have obtained some already, but not nearly enough."{w}
note: NEW: [JP] = 'Meatrif'; [JP] = 'magic airship' (lowercase in running text). [JP] = 'the Dark Kin' as in slice_08 row 621. Selcoa Paint per pilot row 5.

en: "I will not force you.{w}But if you choose to help, we will welcome it.{w}...Even if you are human."{w}
note: Rianna's people are elves ([JP], row 1014).

en: "I will not force you.{w}But if you choose to help, we will welcome it."{w}
"I shall see that the reward is a fitting one."{w}
"Sorry to impose, but would you take this on for me, would you suppose!"{w}
note: Branon asking the party (direction: Branon -> party). Tic doubled for comedy since his [JP] is here a genuine request.

en: "If you are searching, the quickest route is to consult Natori at the Temple of Rafa in Lumisthenes.{w}Now, you are dismissed."{w}
note: Temple of Rafa as in pilot row 1.

en: "Who goes there!{w}Oh, it's you lot."{w}{p}"Have you found the Selcoa Paint?{w}You haven't even found it, and you want an audience with Her Majesty? The nerve!"{w}
note: [JP] -> 'a royal audience' (Rianna's gender not in glossary; avoids Her Majesty). Full-width spaces around the item name dropped. | Accuracy: heika restored as 'Her Majesty' (glossary now female), matching 938.

en: "Who goes there!{w}Oh, it's you lot."{w}{p}"You say you found the Selcoa Paint?{w}Sounds fishy. Show me!{w}...Oh, it's real..."{w}{p}"..........{w}W-well then, I'll take you to see Her Majesty Rianna!{w}Follow me!"{w}
note: [JP] in third person from her subjects -> 'our liege' (gender-neutral). If Rianna is confirmed female (row 949 calls her [JP]), 'Lady Rianna'/'Her Majesty' could replace this. | Accuracy: Rianna-sama from her guard -> 'Her Majesty Rianna' now that the glossary records Rianna as female.

en: "I hear you have obtained the Selcoa Paint..."{w}

"Indeed -- splendid!
Well done. You have my commendation."{w}
note: [JP] = archaic royal 'I deign to praise you'.

en: "Then next, take the Celestial Readings for me.{w}Read the movements of the heavens at the proper place, so that nothing unforeseen befalls us up in the sky."{w}
note: [JP] = 'Celestial Survey Results' (pilot row 6); [JP] = measure it, rendered 'take' (as in taking readings).

en: "For this too, the quickest route is to consult Natori at the Temple of Rafa in Lumisthenes.{w}Now, you are dismissed."{w}
"You lot, back again!?"{w}{p}"Have you taken the Celestial Readings?{w}You haven't even taken them, and you want an audience with Her Majesty? The nerve!"{w}
note: Accuracy: heika restored as 'Her Majesty' (glossary now female), matching 938.

en: "Wh-what, you say you've surveyed the heavens?{w}No way..."{w}{p}"..........{w}All right, follow me."{w}
"Splendid readings.{w}With these, the Meatrif should be able to fly steadily."{w}

note: Source page 2 lacks its closing bracket before {w}{p} (next page opens a new quote) -- treated as a typo; closing quote added. [JP] could be feathers or wings; 'wings' chosen to match 'shining wing'. Wing Soul per pilot row 7. | Editorial: Rianna voice, no contractions (matches 1036 "I am counting on you").

en: "...Our duties keep us from leaving this post.{w}And besides, this kind of work is all we're good for."{w}{p}"Her Majesty Rianna is noble and upright.{w}But for that very reason, she finds it hard to rely on others.{w}Right now, we have no choice but to rely on you."{w}{p}"...It galls me, but please, find the Wing Soul somehow.{w}Carry Her Majesty's wish all the way to the Palace of the Sun."{w}{p}"Please, we're counting on you."{w}
note: Speaker is a guard but speaks for the guards ([JP]), so 'we'. Second [JP] -> 'our liege' to avoid a gendered pronoun. | Accuracy: 'our liege' -> Her Majesty (glossary female); subject of hito ni tayoru koto ga nigate (Rianna) restored as 'she'.

en: The guard bowed low to you.{w}...Then, still bowing, the guard threw you out.{w}
note: [JP]: subject of 'still bowing' read as the guard (topic of the previous sentence); the party is the one thrown out (cf. row 939). Comic: polite bow, still bounced.

en: "You found the Wing Soul!?{w}...All right, we'll call Executor Branon and Madulay!"{w}
note: [JP] -> 'Executor Branon' (title from slice_10 row 765; avoids gendered 'Lord').

en: "You chaps did splendid work, would you suppose!"{w}
"Well, would ya look at this... Ain't no word for it but magnificent!"{w}
note: Madulay: rough artisan speech ([JP], [JP], [JP], [JP]) -> dropped g's, 'ain't', 'ya'.

en: "Mm. Well done, adventurers!"{w}

"Branon, you too
did well to find such talent. You have my thanks."{w}
"What gracious words, would you suppose!"{w}
"Madulay, will it work?"{w}
"Aye, it's spot-on!{w}Shall I go ahead an' fit it in?"{w}
note: Avoided 'yes'm'/'ma'am' (gender).

en:
"Yes, do it.{w}We of Roscadil will take back the sunlight
with our own hands -- without fail!!"{w}
"You lot, go outside the town and wait."{w}
There was a fierce resolve in Rianna's eyes.{w}
"Ohh, it's you chaps!{w}The magic airship will soon be launching, would you suppose!"{w}{p}"Are your preparations complete?"{w}
note: [JP] = sortie/launch.

en: Are you ready?
note: Choice prompt (data).

en:
"Then ought you not get ready quickly,
would you suppose!"{w}
note: Branon answering a 'No' to row 992.

en:
An attempt was made to launch the magic airship, but it would not start
and would not move.{w}
note: Subject of [JP] unstated and not settled (crew or Rianna); passive kept. Source writes [JP] (typo for [JP]); same airship.

en: "Why? Why will it not launch!?"{w}{p}"Madulay! What is going on!?"{w}
note: Editorial: Rianna voice, no contractions.

en: "For some reason the power won't come up -- she won't budge!"{w}
note: 'she' = the ship (nautical), not a person.

en: "What is this!? Begin an inspection at once!"{w}{p}"You lot, forgive me. Give me a little time."{w}
"Not yet!? The magic airship still will not move!?"{w}{p}"You lot, forgive me. Give me a little time."{w}
note: [JP] typo in source, as row 994. | Editorial: Rianna voice, no contractions.

en:
"Her Majesty Rianna should be along
shortly, would you suppose!"{w}
note: [JP] in third person -> 'our liege'. | Accuracy: Rianna-sama -> 'Her Majesty Rianna' (glossary female).

en: "I have kept you waiting!"{w}
"This is the magic airship Meatrif!{w}It took to the air thanks in part to your help.{w}Now, no need to hold back. Come aboard!"{w}
note: Editorial: clunky "It is a ship that..." and ambiguous "too". | Proof: recheck vs source (kyouryoku ... demo aru); 'as well' ambiguous, 'in part' keeps the shared-credit sense.

en: "R-Rianna! Your Majesty!{w}Are you going as well, would you suppose?{w}Is that not dangerous, would you suppose!?"{w}
note: [JP] (direct address, stutter) -> 'R-Rianna! Your Majesty!' to keep the name and the deference without a gendered title.

en:
"I am the head of this nation!
What good am I if I cower before a crisis facing the land!?"{w}
"Branon, I appoint you Minister Extraordinary.{w}While I am away, you will see to domestic affairs."{w}
note: NEW title: [JP] = 'Minister Extraordinary' (alt. 'Special Minister').

en: "Eh? That is... you mean..."{w}
"Mind you get along with the guards, too."{w}

"What joyous words these are, would you suppose...{w}I, Branon, shall protect Roscadil in Your Majesty's
absence, even at the cost of my life, would you suppose!"{w}
"Now, Madulay. Make ready to set sail."{w}
"Aye aye!"{w}
note: [JP] = 'you got it!' in workman's slang.

en:
"We now set course for the Palace of the Sun
aboard the magic airship Meatrif.{w}Let us go, everyone!!"{w}
note: [JP] = everyone (crew and party).

en:
The magic airship Meatrif, which had been flying
smoothly until now, gave a violent lurch.{w}
"...What is happening?"{w}
Elf Soldier
note: NEW name box: [JP].
[JP] as direct address -> 'Your Majesty'.

en: "Blimey... where we're flyin' right now's about as close as we can get."{w}
"Madulay, we will use the magic cannon.{w}That should break through even magic that thick."{w}
note: NEW term: [JP] = 'magic cannon' (parallel to 'magic airship').

en:
"But Majesty, the mana furnace prob'ly won't hold up!{w}Worst case, the second we fire, the furnace blows
an' the ship comes crashin' down!"{w}
note: NEW term: [JP] = 'reactor' (lit. magic perpetual furnace; 'magic reactor' if a fuller form is wanted). [JP] -> 'the reactor'.

en: "So if we do fall, it will be after we have fired?"{w}
note: Rianna asking Madulay; Madulay's 'Don't tell me...' (1020) shows Madulay reads Rianna's intent.

en: "Y-yeah...{w}Don't tell me..."{w}

"All of you, what did you come all this way for!?{w}If we do not act here, sooner or later we will
perish along with the land itself!"{w}
note: [JP] here = Rianna's crew (elf soldiers + Madulay), who answer in 1023-1024, not the party. | Editorial: Rianna voice, no contractions.

en: Elf Soldiers
note: NEW name box: [JP].

en:
"...Your Majesty!
We will follow you to the very end!!"{w}
note: [JP] = anywhere/to the end.

en:
"Phew...
I've followed ya this far on trust.{w}I'll stick with ya right to the end!"{w}
"Good. All of you, to your stations!!"{w}

Rianna briskly issued orders to the
crew, then turned back to face you.{w}
note: [JP] = subordinates; 'crew' since this is aboard the airship.
[JP] = a few people (the party).

en:
"Forgive me, but I cannot leave these
fellows here and head to the Palace of
the Sun myself."{w}{p}"It galls me, but I will wait in Roscadil
with my troops to hear the good
news you bring back."{w}{p}"...Can I count on you?"{w}
note: [JP] = 'these fellows' (her crew). [JP] = Rianna asking the party.

en: "Here goes, Majesty!"{w}

"Everybody grab onto somethin' and hold tight!
Three, two, one...........!"{w}

After a blinding flash and a deafening roar,
the magic airship Meatrif began to shudder.{w}

"Good, go.
We cannot hold this altitude for long."{w}

note: [JP] = croak/kick the bucket -> 'go up in smoke'. [JP] direct address -> 'Majesty'. ''er' = the ship.

en:
"Yes.
We will await the adventurers' return in Roscadil!"{w}
"The rest I leave to you."{w}{p}"I am counting on you to retake the Palace of the Sun."{w}
note: Source has a stray period inside the first quote; normal punctuation used.

en: "Well done, all of you."{w}
note: Post-victory scene starts here (continues into slice_14: Wattner, reward).
Natori: casual and cheerful ([JP] = 'as expected!').

en:
"Congratulations."{w}{p}"This was achieved through the wisdom of
Lady Rianna and the wits of you all, I should say."{w}
note: Mayleen: refined [JP] register. [JP] -> 'Rianna' (no neutral royal title fits Mayleen's polite third-person mention; she is not Rianna's subject). [JP] shared by both -> split 'wisdom'/'wits' for flow. | Accuracy: Rianna-sama in Mayleen's polite mention -> 'Lady Rianna' (glossary female).

en: "You have done splendidly in bringing the light back to the land."{w}{p}"With this, I believe we can rest easy, for the time being at least."{w}
"I shall grant you a reward."{w}

"Well done retaking the Palace of the Sun.{w}Look -- see how the land shines beneath the pouring sunlight."{w}{p}"You have done a great deal for us.{w}But perhaps this was something only adventurers could have accomplished."{w}{p}"...I am grateful.{w}The wait for your safe return felt long indeed."{w}{p}"Now then, let us leave the talk at that.{w}Follow me. It is time for the victory parade."{w}
note: Rianna (Roscadil's ruler, addressed as Your Majesty in slice_13) speaks in a clipped, imperial register throughout; no pronouns used for Rianna (glossary gender unknown).

en: "You did us a great service with the Palace of the Sun.{w}Peace should now come to the land as well.{w}...For a while, at least."{w}

Rianna looked away from you and gazed, squinting against the glare, at the sun shining beyond the window.{w}{p}Her expression seemed filled with a clear sense of accomplishment, and yet somehow lonely.{w}
note: Name repeated instead of a pronoun (gender unknown). | Accuracy: pronoun restored (glossary records Rianna as female).

en:
"How are you all faring?
No trouble since then?"{w}
"Balgert was looking for you, you know."{w}{p}"Head to Algrantz at once."{w}
note: Source typo [JP] read as [JP] (go to).

en: "Fulgrant was looking for you, you know."{w}{p}"Head to Ogre Bay at once."{w}
note: [JP] = Ogre Bay, as in pilot row 160 / slice_10 row 737.

en: "Someone from Perpeco Village was looking for you, you know."{w}{p}"Head to Perpeco Forest at once."{w}
note: Same pattern as slice_10 rows 736-738.

en: "What is it? What is the matter... a package?{w}From Barjeff... a confidential parcel...?{w}...It is big."{w}{p}"Hmph. Well, very well.{w}You have come a long way. Thank you for your trouble.{w}...Now, I do not recall asking for anything..."{w}
note: The party is delivering the parcel from Barjeff (slice_18 row 1396: Barjeff, chief of Teridon, sends a secret parcel to Emperor Rianna). | Editorial: Rianna voice, no contractions.

en: "Blatantly suspicious.{w}I could just burn it as it is...{w}But I suppose I should check what is inside first... --!"{w}
note: Line cut off by a gasp ([JP]) as Barjeff pops out; kept interrupted. | Editorial: Rianna voice, no contractions.

en: Barjeff
note: New name [JP], romanized Barjeff (not in glossary). Chief ([JP]) of Teridon per slice_18. Gender unknown in glossary; no pronouns used.

en: "Riannaaa! I love youuu!{w}HUUUUUUUUGGGGGG!!!"{w}
"You insolent wretch!{w}What do you think you are doing!?"{w}
note: Editorial: Rianna voice, no contractions.

en:
"W-wait wait wait wait wait!
Put the magic gun down, okay!?{w}No violence! Let's settle this with love, I say!"{w}
note: [JP] = "magic gun" (new term; cf. [JP] in slice_13).

en: "It was you who laid hands on me first!{w}And now, of all times, you make excuses!?{w}What you have done deserves ten thousand deaths!!"{w}{p}"Now submit quietly and be cut down by my own hand, here and now!"{w}
note: [JP] = a lord personally executing an offender; rendered "cut down by my own hand". | Editorial: Rianna voice, no contractions.

en: "I told you to wait!{w}Ah, I see now -- you've been blinded by my love! It's me, Barjeff!"{w}{p}"You said it yourself before, didn't you!?{w}'Let's see you export this so-called love of yours!'{w}So here I am, doing just that--!"{w}
note: [JP] rendered with single quotes as a quoted remark. [JP] (old-fashioned) gives Barjeff a slightly pompous ring.

en: "...I know full well it is you.{w}Is that supposed to be a problem?"{w}
note: [JP] = she knows it is Barjeff and is going to punish anyway. Rendered as knowing who it is; could also be read as "I am well aware (of what I said)". | Editorial: Rianna voice, no contractions.

en: "So that you bring no shame on the name of Teridon,{w}I shall erase you without a trace.{w}
note: No closing quote in source; the next row repeats this text inside {0E}..{0F}. [JP] romanized Teridon (new place name, the TRD town).
{0E}..{0F} repeats row 1059 with {w} -> \n, as in source. [JP] = punishment shout, rendered "Perish!".

en: "I may die, but love is immortal!{w}
note: No closing quote in source; repeated in next row.

en:
{0E}"I may die, but love is immortal!{0F}
GYAAAAAAAAAAAAAH!"{w}
"Ship this piece of garbage back to Teridon at once.{w}...Incidentally."{w}
"Do not tell me you knew of this farce and...{w}
note: No closing quote in source; repeated in next row. Line trails off deliberately. | Editorial: Rianna voice, no contractions; 1065 echo kept identical.

en:
{0E}"Do not tell me you knew of this farce and...{0F}
...Heh. A foolish question.{w}Thank you for your trouble."{w}
note: [JP] left as ambiguous as the source (obviously knew / obviously did not). | Editorial: echo of 1064 updated to match.

en: "...I stayed true... to love...{w}My life... was a good one..."{w}{p}"...You adventurers... think so too... don't you?{w}Cherish... love..."{w}
"Slump."{w}
note: [JP] is spoken aloud (Barjeff voices his own collapse, a gag); rendered as a spoken sound word.

en:
Lumisthenes was nothing like its usual self.
The city had suddenly been attacked by the forces of darkness, and people were being set upon everywhere.{w}{p}The screams of panic-stricken people rang out from every direction.{w}{p}Among them, a familiar cry reached your ears.{w}
note: [JP] = "the forces of darkness" (new term).

en: Decoy
note: Glossary spelling.

en:
"Waaah!!
Stay the hell awaaaay!!"{w}

"A magic puppet, is it...
A rather unsatisfying quarry for the pleasure of taking a life... but no matter."{w}
note: [JP] = "magic puppet" (new term; what Decoy is). | Editorial: "Hardly satisfying prey for the pleasure" was garbled.

en:
"Whoa whoa whoa, rethink this!!
You won't get nothin' tasty outta eatin' me-e-e!"{w}
note: Decoy uses rough [JP]/[JP] speech; rendered with dropped g's and slang.

en: Shaharon's dark hand reached out toward the cowering Decoy.{w}
With a flash of a white blade, a young swordswoman with a magnificent beard stepped in front of Shaharon, barring the way.{w}
note: [JP] = young (girl) swordswoman, stated by the source itself; no pronoun needed. This is Milonya (next name box).

en: Milonya
note: Glossary spelling.

en: "What do you think you're doing to my darling Decoykins!?!"{w}
note: [JP] -> "Decoykins" throughout (English diminutive for the doting [JP]; the project does not use -chan). Neighbouring slices (15, 16) should adopt the same.

en: "Decoykins, now that Milonya's here, everything's gonna be A-OK!"{w}
note: Milonya refers to herself by name ([JP]); kept. [JP] in katakana -> "A-OK".

en: "...Uh."{w}{p}"Th-thanks..."{w}
note: [JP] before [JP] read as a hesitant start; "Uh" + stammered "Th-thanks" keeps both readings.

en:
"S-so cuuute!
Aaah, I wanna make you my briiide!!"{w}
note: [JP]: want to take Decoy as a bride (gag on Milonya being the suitor). Read as addressed to Decoy; could be an aside.

en:
"Heh, what a racket...
But this may prove rather entertaining."{w}

"What?
This shadow..."{w}
A huge shadow fell over the entire city.{w}Looking up at the sky, you saw a silver dragon soaring serenely overhead.{w}
note: [JP] = "silver dragon".

en:
"So the primeval dragon sees fit to interfere...
I shall withdraw for now."{w}{p}"It seems your kind has the gall to scheme an assault on our stronghold, but it is futile."{w}{p}"After all, even the Moonlight Spirit wishes for us to take hold of the sun."{w}
note: The schemer in [JP] is unstated; rendered "your kind" (whoever stands before Shaharon: the party / Milonya / the townsfolk). [JP] = Moonlight Spirit (slice_02/05). | Editorial: "would interfere" read as conditional; clarity.

en: The forces of darkness vanished along with Shaharon, like a receding wave.{w}{p}As if it had been watching to see this through, the silver dragon flying overhead also rose up into a break in the clouds and passed from sight.{w}
Gradually, quiet returned to the city, and you headed to the Temple of Rafa.{w}
note: [JP] = Temple of Rafa (pilot row 1, slice_09).

en: You asked Natori about the dragon that had appeared in the sky over the city, and about the Moonlight Spirit Shaharon had mentioned before leaving.{w}

"A silver dragon?
One so mighty the monsters turned tail...{w}Oh! Maybe it's...!"{w}

"Could it be Agintaitus, the dragon of myth?
The legends do mention a silver dragon."{w}
note: New name [JP] romanized Agintaitus (possibly from Romanian argint "silver" -> Argintaitus; flagged). Also in slice_16 row 1231.

en:
"But it's a creature of myth, so I can't really say for sure."{w}{p}"And the Moonlight Spirit... I think that means Yorfa, who governs the moon, but I don't know much more than the name myself."{w}{p}"Sorry.
If I knew more, I'd love to tell you..."{w}
note: [JP]: honorific dropped ("Lady" would assume gender).

en:
"Hmm...
Oh! Maybe this is exactly when you should go ask Council Chair Wattner!"{w}{p}"The Chair just might know something."{w}
note: [JP] = Council Chair (slice_09 row 684). Subject of [JP] = the party (next row they go to Wattner). | Accuracy: kikite miru beki kamo ne -- the 'kamo' hedge restored.

en: You spoke to Wattner, who was busy handling the aftermath at the Central Council.{w}
note: [JP] = Central Council (new term).

en:
"A giant silver dragon, you say...
Then it is almost certainly the great dragon Agintaitus."{w}{p}"I have heard that it is the guardian of a place called the Castle of the Wind, which has floated in the sky since ancient times. They say it has watched over this world since time long past."{w}{p}"As for the Castle of the Wind, you would do better to ask Mayleen at the Observatory than me."{w}
note: [JP] = Castle of the Wind, [JP] = Observatory (new terms).

en: You asked Wattner to tell you about Yorfa, the Moonlight Spirit, as well.{w}

"Yorfa, the Moonlight Spirit?
...Well now, I'm afraid I don't know."{w}
note: [JP] may be evasive (next row: nothing more could be gotten out of Wattner); "Well now" keeps that hint without stating it.

en:
It seemed you would get nothing more out of Wattner.
You headed to the Observatory.{w}

"The Castle of the Wind, where the ancient dragon Agintaitus dwells?
That castle floats inside a great thundercloud, so there is no way to get there."{w}{p}"I hear the elven nation is building a ship that flies through the sky, but they would never lend it out for a mere survey."{w}
note: [JP] = "the elven nation" (presumably Rianna's Roscadil; left unnamed as in source). Mayleen keeps her refined register.

en: "...Well, if you were swept up in a tornado or some such and lucky enough to land there, that would be another matter..."{w}
A storm blew in out of nowhere.{w}The storm was shaped like a small doll and a bearded swordfighter.{w}
note: Source lacks the final [JP]; period added.

en: "GYAAAH!"{w}
note: Speaker ??? (Decoy, unseen yet).

en: "Waaait, Decoykiiins!"{w}
note: Speaker ??? (Milonya).

en: "Get away! Stay the hell away from me!{w}You... you Beard Girl!{w}Die! Die, or turn into a beard!"{w}
note: [JP] = "Beard Lady" (Decoy's insult; recurs in slice_15).

en:
"Aww, come on, Decoykins!
Call me by my proper name -- Milonya!"{w}

"GYAAAH!{w}I said quit comin' over here!
Get back! Don't touch me! Stop rubbin' up on meee!"{w}
note: [JP] = rubbing cheeks/body against someone affectionately.

en: "Decoykiiins!{w}Aaah! The way you run away is just so pretty-witty!!"{w}
note: [JP] (baby-talk "pretty") -> "pretty-witty".

en: "...*SPURT!* (nosebleed)"{w}
note: [JP] = spurting sound; stage direction [JP] kept in parentheses. Same line recurs in slice_15 rows 1139/1141. | Editorial: nosebleed sound unified as *SPURT* (1109/1139/1141); 1109 keeps the source "!".

en: The storm passed.{w}Left behind were copious bloodstains, suggesting some terrible tragedy,{w}{p}and yet,{w}the people who had seen the whole thing were going about their day as if nothing had happened.{w}{p}Apparently this was an everyday occurrence.{w}
note: The sentence runs across the page break in the source; cut at the same point.

en:
"Oh, excuse me!
Have you seen Decoykins?{w}...I'm sure Decoykins is around here somewhere..."{w}{p}"Who's Decoykins, you ask? Oh...
I'm sorry! I just assumed you were from this town.{w}Decoykins is cute and teeny-tiny and..."{w}{p}"...and the way Decoykins scampers around is just too cute!
Who knew something so pretty-witty existed in this world!{w}Aaah... I just can't help myself!{w}
note: No closing quote in source; kept. Decoy named instead of a pronoun (gender unknown). The second page answers an implied question from the party. | Accuracy: 'Dekoi-chan desu ka?' is Milonya echoing the party's implied question, not asking it herself; 'you ask' keeps the direction.

en: "Oh, it's the adventurers from the other day!{w}Decoykins ran off on me again...{w}If you see Decoykins, please let me know!"{w}
"...? My name? Like I said, it's Decoyki...?{w}
note: Speaker ????? = Milonya before being named; she starts to give Decoy's name instead of her own. No closing quote; repeated in next rows.

en:
{0E}"...? My name? Like I said, it's Decoyki...?{0F}
Oh, I'm so sorry! I was so wrapped up in Decoykins!{w}
"Beard Girl, more like!!"{w}
note: [JP] = "you mean Beard Lady".

en: Milonya
note: Source name box reads [JP] (a typo for [JP]); rendered with the glossary spelling Milonya.

en:
"Oh, found you, Decoykins!
Waaait! Let me snuggle all that fluff!"{w}
note: Speaker field shows the typo name [JP]; same character. [JP] = fluffy cuddling.

en:
"You! Stay away from me!
Hey, what's the deal with law and order in this town!?"{w}
note: Decoy fleeing Milonya; tema = 'you' (hostile), aimed at Milonya.

en:
"Hellooo, everyone!
Am I not looking for Decoykins today, you ask?{w}I already had my fill just now! ...Guheh~"{w}
note: Decoy-chan rendered 'Decoykins' throughout (Milonya's doting -chan); the party's question is implied by -tte?; guhe-heart giggle -> 'Guheh~' (no ASCII music note).

en: "Oh, this beard?{w}My master gave it to me."{w}{p}"Master said something really complicated about it, but{w}

note: New name Shimerief (romanized). 'Sono hige-sugata' kept as 'the bearded look' (whose look is unstated). Master referred to without pronouns. | Accuracy: pronoun restored for Shimerief (glossary female).

en:
"GYAAH! Oh, it's you guys!
Don't you dare tell anyone I came this way!? I mean it!?{w}Later!!"{w}

note: Name-mangled call kept as stretched 'Deee-cooy-kiiins'. Interrupted 'nameh...' (lick) kept as a cut-off 'I'd lick... ahem'.

en:
"I know! I've thought of something!{w}If Decoykins keeps running away, then a trap's the answer!
I just have to catch the little darling!"{w}
note: Object of torae- (catch) is Decoy by context; 'the little darling' avoids repeating the name and a pronoun.

en: "I call it... the Decoykins-Only Trap!"{w}
note: Decorative star between the words dropped (ASCII only).

en:
"Hey, you guys! What are you scheming!?
Don't you DARE help with anything like that!{w}I mean it!"{w}
note: Editorial: Decoy addresses the party as "you guys" (1124, 1142, 1144); "you lot" is the guards'/Rianna's/Shimerief's word.

en: "Deee-cooy-kiiiiiiiins------!!"{w}

"GYAAAAH!
Die! Die and then die some more!"{w}
note: Shinde shine (lit. 'die by dying') = doubled curse; full force kept.

en:
"Run around while you still can!
Decoykiiins!!"{w}

"Everyone! Look at this, look!{w}So I used the capture trap, right,
and inside there was a letter from Decoykins!"{w}
note: 'Hokaku torappu' = the goblin item (ITEM_PRIZ 54, a magic-puppet capture trap); kept generic lowercase.

en: You think I'm some pushover, moron?{w}Die.{w}Die twice.{w}
note: Decoy's letter (no quote marks in source, so none here). Namete n no ka = 'are you making a fool of me'; full rudeness kept.

en:
"That's what it says!{w}And this squiggly handwriting, like a worm
crawled across the page, is just too cute!"{w}

"...Master was right all along.{w}Against cuteness that deadly, it doesn't matter
whether your sword is strong or weak!"{w}
note: Read as Master's teaching (cf. ITEM_TEXT 704: the false beard is Shimerief's graduation gift to Milonya).

en: "Cuteness is mightier than the sword!{w}Ahh, Decoykiiins!!"{w}
".........*SPURT* (nosebleed)"{w}
note: Sound effect bushi! + stage direction (hanaji) translated. | Editorial: nosebleed sound unified as *SPURT* (matches 1109, 1110 "spurting").

en:
"I'm keeping that letter as my treasure!
I get a new letter every time I set the trap!{w}Ahh, Decoykiiins!!"{w}
"...*SPURT* (nosebleed)"{w}
note: Editorial: nosebleed sound unified as *SPURT*.
Decoy says boukensha in katakana (childish/garbled); rendered as a mangled 'ad-ven-churers'.

en: "Don't be such a drag! C'mon, what's the harm!"{w}

note: Decoy (a puppet) mistakes haircuts for heads changing shape; kept literal.
Kata ni nosero: Decoy asks to be lifted onto the listener's shoulder.
Kao no = facial hair, matching 'the stuff on your head' in 1147.

en: "Ow! Hey, don't drop me!{w}

{0E}"Ow! Hey, don't drop me!{0F}
...Huh? ...Did it hurt that bad?{w}

note: Hige-onna = Decoy's insult for Milonya, 'Beard Girl'. 'Beard Girl's' = her beard (the false beard). Echo repeats 1150 visibly.

en:
"...Sorry, okay? Are you mad?
...You're not mad?{w}

note: 'Sore' = the item the party is holding (row 1144).

en:
"Aww, I can't have it, huh... Hmm...{w}Hmm? Why do I want hair?{w}...It's to scare off that Beard Girl."{w}{p}"If all she does is go 'cute, cute!' at me,
then I just gotta not be cute, right?{w}If I stuck on a beard like that Beard Girl has..."{w}
note: Pronoun for Milonya avoided by repeating the nickname. | Accuracy: source leaves the subject (Milonya) unnamed here; 'she' restored now that the glossary records Milonya as female (the next sentence still names 'that Beard Girl', as the source does).

en:
"Hey, you know Joker Land?{w}I hear the clowns have a makeup room there.{w}Could you bring me something from it?"{w}{p}"Lemme think...
just a beard, and I might still lose...{w}Beard Glasses! Gimme some Beard Glasses!"{w}
note: Source typo 'arashii' read as 'aru rashii'. Hige-megane (novelty glasses with nose and mustache, ITEM_PRIZ 53) = 'Beard Glasses' to keep the beard motif; item name not yet fixed elsewhere.

en: "I mean, look at this body of mine, right?{w}If I walked, who knows how many days it'd take...{w}C'mon, I'm counting on ya, best buddy!!"{w}
note: Shinyuu = 'best buddy' (Decoy's chummy address to the party).

en: "Okay, I'm counting on ya, best buddy!"{w}

"Whoa, you guys are the best!"{w}{p}"With these, that Beard Girl won't come at me going
'So cute!' anymore! Pretty awesome, huh!"{w}{p}"I'm gonna go try 'em right now!"{w}

note: Dots converted 2 ellipsis chars -> '...'. Narration window (Decoy's scream offscreen).

en: "...Hah... hah... That was a close one...{w}That freak went 'Soooo cute!' while spurting blood...{w}It totally backfired..."{w}
note: Yarou (crude 'that bastard') aimed at Milonya; 'that freak' keeps the insult without gendering.

en:
"Yo, best buddy! Anything fun happen lately?
If there was, tell m"{w}
note: Source cuts off mid-word (oshie-); English cut mid-word too, interrupted by Milonya.

en: "Decoykiiiiiiiins!!"{w}
"Whoa! Get lost! Get away from meee!{w}GYAAH"{w}
Lumisthenes is peaceful again today.{w}
Lotz
note: New name: Lotz (rottsu), goblin elder of the Jakobis Spell Hall. Gender unknown: no 'old man' used.

en: "Oho, you've come all the way from Algrantz.{w}Lumisthenes is a place where wisdom gathers,{w}so take your time and look around."{w}
note: Editorial: "This Lumisthenes" calque.

en: "But... traveler from Algrantz,{w}I'm ashamed to say this shop has no wares at present.{w}Take home an old-timer's stories instead, if you would."{w}
"Forgive me for not introducing myself sooner.{w}I am Lotz, of this Jakobis Spell Hall."{w}
note: New name: Jakobis Spell Hall (Jakobis jutsuhoudou; also HELP_TEXT 110 town facility).

en: "We goblins, like the ogres,{w}set great store by a closed society.{w}But that alone will not do."{w}{p}"There is much that we cannot do.{w}And conversely, there is much that only we can do.{w}And from mingling, new things are born, too."{w}

"The role of the old is to pass things on...{w}If there is anything you don't understand, ask me any time."{w}{p}"But only after you have thought it through yourselves.{w}Relying on my knowledge is all well and good,{w}but it is you young ones who will build the future."{w}{p}"Never forget that, hm?"{w}{p}"Knowledge, they say, is a treasure without form.{w}However much you gather and keep, it is never a burden,{w}and it never vanishes. So learn."{w}

"Traveler from Algrantz,{w}I would ask you to hear an old-timer's request."{w}{p}"You know this shop has nothing in it.{w}...The other day, I thought the goods had finally arrived,{w}but all that came was an empty wagon and a dying peddler..."{w}{p}"Never mind the goods. But...{w}

note: New name: Mujirod (romanized; ITEM_PRIZ 55 spells it 'Mujiddo' -- likely a typo there). Shahon = hand copy. Yakara = 'ruffians', reused in 1178/1180. | Accuracy: hearsay -souda restored (Lotz heard it from the survivor, cf. 1175).

en: "I haven't much time left myself.{w}To come across a work by Mujirod again...{w}a chance like that will never come twice."{w}{p}"Will you do this for me?"{w}
"The ruffians headed for the Crotoa City Ruins,{w}or so I heard from someone who survived.{w}I'm... counting on you."{w}
"All things come down to fate, true. Even so,{w}if one can draw it in with one's own hands,{w}how could one not?"{w}
note: En = fate/karmic ties; impersonal 'one' kept since it is a maxim (probably Lotz's reply if the party hesitates).

en: "Thank you. I'm truly grateful.{w}I had resigned myself to never having it again."{w}

"Still, it has come back in fine condition.
...So one of those ruffians understood this book's worth.{w}Would you pass a message on to them for me? 'Any time.'"{w}
note: Lotz invites the thief to visit; 'them' = the unnamed ruffian(s) (gender-neutral). | Editorial: tangled punctuation ".'?" untangled. | Proof: idiom fix ('pass a word on').

en:
"Knowledge is a treasure without form,
so it belongs equally to all who see its worth.{w}They will be most welcome."{w}

"............Heh. No... forgive me.{w}I just remembered that I had been calling such a person a 'ruffian.'
A funny thing..."{w}
note: Source quotes the word in single brackets; kept as 'ruffian.'

en:
"It seems there is still much I do not know.{w}Traveler from Algrantz,
I am no longer young enough to travel."{w}{p}"But..."{w}{p}"If you find anything rare,
would you bring it here, if only to humor
an old-timer who hasn't long left?"{w}
"As it happens, this shop has nothing in it right now.{w}I look forward to it livening up."{w}

"Traveler from Algrantz,
welcome indeed.{w}Make yourself at home."{w}

note: Fame: glossary term. 'Fame ni hikari wo yadosu' = turning Fame into compass light (cf. slice_16 row 1220).

en: "I hope you find the Three Phantom Stones!{w}I'm rooting for you!"{w}
note: Sangenseki = 'Three Phantom Stones' (slice_01/02 usage); slice_09 used 'Three Mystic Stones' -- needs harmonising.

en:
"Seeing karma is what a fortune-teller does,
but we can read other people's, never our own.{w}

note: Inga = karma/cause and effect; generic 'we' for fortune-tellers, 'I' for Natori's own greed.

en:
"There are two kinds of fortune-telling, you know.{w}Either you listen to someone's troubles,
or you look into that person's destiny."{w}
"Either way, it's all up to the person...{w}Sigh... my reading said red, though...{w}Why did it have to be black..."{w}
note: Red/black = roulette (Natori gambles at the casino, slice_16).

en: "............Are they cheating or something?"{w}
note: Ikasama = the casino rigging the game; subject 'they' restored.

en:
"Heh heh heh, just as foretold.{w}I knew you would come.{w}And that you would grant my wish, too, hm?"{w}{p}"No, no, I don't need to hear your answer!{w}You're going to bring me
the Dice of Fate, aren't you?"{w}{p}"My next big bet is riding on it!{w}
note: Unmei no daisu = 'Dice of Fate' (ITEM 467, alchemy item; name not yet fixed elsewhere).

en:
{0E}"My next big bet is riding on it!{0F}
I'm counting on you, 'kay!"{w}

"Any time is fine.{w}I know my luck will be at its very best
the moment you bring me the Dice of Fate!"{w}
"I'm countin' on youuu!"{w}
note: Decorative star dropped (ASCII).

en: "Heh heh, I knew it all along...{w}that you would come today...{w}Thank you. Today, I'm going to..."{w}
note: Sentence continues into 1196 ('WIN!!'); cut at the matching point.

en: "WIN!!"{w}

"...I'm back.{w}They said no bringing in your own dice,
and threw me out... Boo hoo..."{w}{p}"Guess you really can't cheat after all...{w}My luck was supposed to be at its very best... and yet...?{w}

note: Continues in slice_16 row 1200 ('I should've just played normally!').
